hypothesis.title: currency 2.0.4 rollout introduced conversion latency regression
hypothesis.summary: Currency service was deployed to version 2.0.4 nineteen minutes before the alert. Immediately after, currency p95 latency jumped from 6ms to 904ms and currency began logging "conversion took longer than expected" errors. Frontend calls currency on most requests, so the 950ms added latency in currency propagated upstream, causing frontend p95 to breach 1s. Currency shows no resource saturation (CPU 15%, memory 22%), indicating a code-level performance regression in the new version.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on frontend latency, but errors and latency propagate upstream from their origin. The trace analysis shows currency accounts for 100% of the added latency (+950ms) in frontend traces. Currency's own p95 latency spiked from 6ms to 904ms starting around -15m, matching the frontend latency spike timeline. Currency logs show 456 ERROR messages "conversion took longer than expected" starting -19m, which aligns with the currency deployment of version 2.0.4 that occurred -19m before the alert. The currency service itself shows no resource pressure: CPU is only 15%, memory is 22%, and error rate remains stable at 0.4%. This pattern—a deployment followed immediately by latency spike and error logs about slow operations, without resource saturation—strongly indicates the new version introduced a performance regression. The cart changes (deploy at -17m, config at -7m) are red herrings: cart's own p95 latency remains flat at 25ms, and cart is not on the critical path shown in the slow traces. The valkey-cart restart (exit 137, likely OOMKilled) occurred much earlier and cart metrics show no ongoing issues.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: Currency rolled out to 2.0.4 at -19m, exactly when the latency spike and error logs began, establishing temporal causation.
Currency p95 latency jumped from 6ms to 904ms starting -15m, a 150× increase that matches the timeline of the deployment.
456 ERROR logs 'conversion took longer than expected' starting -19m confirm currency itself is experiencing slow operations, not just reporting them.
Trace analysis shows currency accounts for 100% of the added latency (+950ms) in frontend traces, proving currency is the origin, not a victim.
Currency CPU remains at 15% (peak 17%), ruling out CPU saturation as the mechanism and pointing to inefficient code in the new version.
Cart p95 latency remains flat at 25ms despite its own deploy and config change, ruling out cart changes as the cause.

suggested_actions.title: Roll back currency to version 2.0.2
suggested_actions.rationale: Version 2.0.2 was stable before the rollout. Undo will restore the previous ReplicaSet and immediately resolve the latency regression.

suggested_actions.title: Verify currency latency returns to baseline
suggested_actions.command: kubectl exec -n otel-demo deploy/currency -- curl -s localhost:8080/health && watch 'kubectl top pod -n otel-demo -l app=currency'
suggested_actions.rationale: After rollback, confirm currency p95 latency drops back to ~6ms and frontend latency recovers to <200ms within 2-3 minutes.

suggested_actions.title: Inspect currency 2.0.4 conversion logic for performance regression
suggested_actions.rationale: Review the diff between 2.0.2 and 2.0.4 for changes to currency conversion code—likely an inefficient algorithm, blocking I/O, or missing cache that causes the 150× slowdown.

alternatives.why_less_likely: Cart deployed to 2.0.3 at -17m and had a config change at -7m, but cart's own p95 latency remains flat at 25ms and cart is not present in the slow frontend traces. The cart changes are coincidental.

retrieved_documents.title: Cart / Valkey errors and timeouts
retrieved_documents.snippet: Decide whether the problem is the client pool or the server. - Server: `kubectl -n otel-demo exec deploy/valkey-cart -- valkey-cli --latency` and `SLOWLOG GET 10`. High latency or `BUSY` => datastore degradation. - Client: server latency flat but cart logs `pool busy=N/N` or "timeout awaiting connection" => pool exhaustion. Raise the pool size and restart cart.

retrieved_documents.title: Ad service CPU saturation slowed every product page
retrieved_documents.snippet: ## Summary A regex in ad targeting went quadratic on long keyword lists. A small share of ad calls hit DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. ## Resolution Scaled ad to 4 replicas, then fixed the regex. ## Lessons - CPU at limit + `CPUThrottlingHigh` + latency on one service with no errors elsewhere = sa…

retrieved_documents.title: CrashLoopBackOff triage
retrieved_documents.snippet: 1. `kubectl -n otel-demo logs <pod> --previous` shows why the last start failed. 2. Missing env var / config file / bad command -> check the most recent config change or rollout. 3. If a rollout caused it: `kubectl -n otel-demo rollout undo deployment/<svc>`. 4. If an env var changed: restore it with `kubectl set env`.
